# handlr-app

> The full-stack Handlr app skeleton — the starting point for a server-driven web app:
> an HTMX + Handlebars + Tailwind frontend over a PHP Pipe + Handler backend. Scaffold
> it, then build features by dropping a service provider into a domain folder. This
> file orients an AI or a developer building on it: what goes where, and how to run it.

Composer package `phillipsharring/handlr-app`. Scaffold a new project:

```bash
composer create-project phillipsharring/handlr-app my-app
# a post-create hook runs `npm install` in the frontend half
```

The result is **two sibling halves** in one repo — `backend/` (composer) and
`frontend/` (npm) — talking over HTTP. Run them side by side:

```bash
cd backend  && composer run dev   # PHP API on http://localhost:8000
cd frontend && npm run dev        # Vite on http://localhost:5173, proxies /api → :8000
```

## The packages under this skeleton (read these next)

Each package ships its own `llms.txt` — the authoritative map for that layer:

- Backend framework (Pipe/Handler, routing, authorization, DB): [../backend/llms.txt](../backend/llms.txt)
- Frontend runtime (HTMX toolkit, declarative behavior, modals/toasts): [../frontend/llms.txt](../frontend/llms.txt)
- Build tooling (pages/layouts/components → static HTML): [../build/llms.txt](../build/llms.txt)

Full prose docs: https://handlr.dev/

## Commands (composer scripts — there is no `handlr` binary)

Run from `backend/`. These are wired in `backend/composer.json` and call the vendored
framework scripts:

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `composer run dev` | serve the API (`php -S localhost:8000 -t public`) |
| `composer run test` | run the Pest suite |
| `composer run migrate` | run the next migration batch |
| `composer run migrate:fresh` | drop everything and re-run migrations |
| `composer run seed` / `seed:fresh` | seed (optionally truncate first) |
| `composer run fresh` | `migrate:fresh && seed:fresh` — reset the dev DB |
| `composer run make:record\|table\|handler\|pipe\|scaffold` | scaffold a piece (args forwarded) |
| `composer run make:migration <name>` / `make:seed <name>` | scaffold schema/seed |
| `composer run module:install -- <name>` | install both halves of a module |

Frontend (`npm run` in `frontend/`): `dev`, `build`, `preview`.

## Directory layout

```
my-app/
├── backend/
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── routes.php          # declares the cross-cutting JUNCTIONS once (CORS/session/CSRF/auth)
│   │   ├── config.php          # app config + the `providers` list (this is the wiring)
│   │   └── <Domain>/           # one folder per feature domain, each with a ServiceProvider
│   ├── bootstrap.php           # locates the app root, boots the Kernel
│   ├── migrations/             # {timestamp}_{desc}.php
│   ├── seeds/                  # seed files
│   ├── public/index.php        # web entrypoint
│   ├── resources/views/        # server-side PHP views (for straight-HTMX / ViewPipe)
│   └── composer.json           # the command surface above
└── frontend/
    ├── content/{layouts,components,pages}/   # the HTML the build compiles
    ├── src/app.js              # entry: imports htmx + `/init`, registers helpers, builds window.App
    ├── src/namespace.js        # assembles window.App from handlr-frontend exports
    ├── modules/                # local frontend modules (each a dir with a module.js)
    ├── site.config.js          # [[placeholders]] + the `modules` list
    └── vite.config.js          # tailwind + the handlr-build dev plugin
```

The skeleton ships with `Auth` (login/signup/password-reset/email-verify, RBAC) and
`Profile` domains already built — read them as worked examples.

## Building a feature — where things go

The one hard rule: a feature is a **service provider** listed in `app/config.php`'s
`providers` array. It ties routes, events, migrations, and bindings into the framework.
Everything else below is the **recommended** convention (the shipped `Auth` and
`Profile` domains follow it), **not dictated** — see "Layout is a suggestion."

A domain folder groups a feature's pieces. For example, a `Checklists` domain
(illustrating the handlr 0.15 `resolves()->policy()` flow):

```
backend/app/Checklists/
├── ChecklistsServiceProvider.php     # routes(), events(), boot() registers resolution
├── Domain/
│   ├── ChecklistRecord.php           # the Record (@property docblocks over $data)
│   ├── ChecklistPolicy.php           # object-level authorization (consult → Grant/Deny)
│   └── ChecklistAction.php           # enum ChecklistAction implements PolicyAction
├── Data/
│   ├── ChecklistsTable.php           # the Table gateway
│   └── ChecklistsQuery.php           # custom read SQL (ownership checks, etc.)
├── Inputs/ChecklistInput.php         # validated HandlerInput (validateForCreate/Update)
├── UpdateChecklist/
│   ├── PatchUpdateChecklist.php      # the Pipe (HTTP: build input, guard, call handler)
│   └── UpdateChecklistHandler.php    # the Handler (pure logic, no HTTP)
├── Items/ …                          # more feature folders (one per endpoint group)
└── Listeners/ …                      # event listeners (Handlers on an event name)
```

"Build me a pipe that does X" resolves to:

| Piece | Where | Registered by |
|---|---|---|
| Endpoint (Pipe + Handler + Input) | `app/<Domain>/<Feature>/` | `provider->routes()` attaches the Pipe into a junction |
| Persistent shape | `app/<Domain>/Domain/<X>Record.php` + `Data/<X>Table.php` | used by handlers; resolution via `ResolutionRegistry` in `boot()` |
| Object authorization | `app/<Domain>/Domain/<X>Policy.php` + `<X>Action.php` | `->resolves(XRecord::class)->policy(XAction::Edit)` on the route |
| Reaction to something | `app/<Domain>/Listeners/<X>Listener.php` | `provider->events()` map |
| The whole feature | `app/<Domain>/<Domain>ServiceProvider.php` | added to `app/config.php` `providers` |

A route attaches to a **junction** declared in `app/routes.php` — `api.authed`,
`api.admin`, etc. — so a provider inherits the session/CSRF/auth stack without
redeclaring it:

```php
public function routes(Router $router): void
{
    $router->intoJunction('api.authed')
        ->group('/widgets/{id:uuid}')
            ->resolves(WidgetRecord::class)->policy(WidgetAction::View)   // group default
            ->get('', [GetWidget::class])
            ->patch('', [UpdateWidget::class])->policy(WidgetAction::Edit)
        ->end();
}
```

The resolve pipe loads the record, consults the policy, and injects the record into the
handler by type hint — so an unauthorized request never reaches your code. See the
[backend authorization docs](https://handlr.dev/backend/authorization).

## Layout is a suggestion, not a mandate

The DDD-ish domain grouping above is one way. The framework does **not** dictate folder
structure — the only requirement is a registered service provider. Organizing by *type*
of thing works just as well:

```
backend/app/
├── Db/Records/ , Db/Tables/
├── Pipes/ , Handlers/ , Listeners/ , Policies/ , Inputs/
└── WidgetsServiceProvider.php
```

The pieces (Pipe, Handler, Record, Table, Policy, Listener) are intentionally granular —
they compose in an opinionated way, but where you *put* them is up to the team. Pick a
convention and keep it consistent; the domain-folder layout is recommended mainly
because it keeps a feature's files together and makes a provider easy to find.

## The frontend side of a feature

A page is an HTML file in `frontend/content/pages/` that renders the API via a
Handlebars `<template>`; auth-gated content uses `data-requires-auth` +
`hx-trigger="auth-load"`. `src/app.js` wires the runtime (`/init`) and builds
`window.App` (from `src/namespace.js`) so inline scripts can call
`App.ui.openFormModal(...)`, `App.ui.toast.show(...)`, etc. See the
[frontend docs](https://handlr.dev/frontend/) and [../frontend/llms.txt](../frontend/llms.txt).

## Worked examples to learn from

The best references are the domains this skeleton ships with — read them, they follow
every convention above:

- **`app/Auth/`** — login, signup, password reset, email verification, RBAC. Shows the
  domain layout at scale (`Data/`, `Domain/`, feature folders, `Listeners/`, events).
- **`app/Profile/`** — a smaller domain: pipes + handlers + one input + a provider.

When in doubt, mirror those and the routing/authorization patterns in the
[docs](https://handlr.dev/) and the [backend llms.txt](../backend/llms.txt).
